facts.statement: Psarolepis was an extinct genus of bony fish that lived between 418 and 397 million years ago during the Pridoli and Lochkovian stages.
facts.quote: Psarolepis (; psārolepis, from Greek ψαρός 'speckled' and λεπίς 'scale') is an extinct monospecific genus of bony fish which lived from around 418 to 397 million years ago (Pridoli to Lochkovian stages).

facts.statement: Fossils of Psarolepis were primarily found in South China and the genus was described by paleontologist Xiaobo Yu in 1998.
facts.quote: Fossils of Psarolepis have been found mainly in South China and described by paleontologist Xiaobo Yu in 1998.

facts.statement: Psarolepis possessed a unique feature called 'parasymphysical tooth whorls,' where teeth extended upward at the front of the lower jaw.
facts.quote: Psarolepis had a pair of 'parasymphysical tooth whorls', teeth which extend up at the front of the lower jaw.

facts.statement: The head of Psarolepis was constructed from several thick dermal plates covered in deep pock-marks and large pores.
facts.quote: The head was made of several thick dermal plates and covered with deep pock-marks and large pores.

facts.statement: The pock-marked head plates of Psarolepis contained a layer of porcelain-like material known as cosmine.
facts.quote: The pock-marked head of Psarolepis was made of plates containing a layer of porcelain-like cosmine.

facts.statement: Psarolepis had a strangely humped snout with nostrils positioned above the eyes, which were located just above the upper jaw.
facts.quote: The snout was strangely humped and the nostrils were located above the eyes, which were just above the upper jaw.

facts.statement: The premaxilla and dentary bones of Psarolepis featured large inner teeth alongside an irregular array of tiny outer teeth.
facts.quote: The premaxilla and the dentary had large inner teeth and irregular array of tiny outer teeth.

facts.statement: The fin spines found in Psarolepis are characteristic of primitive jawed fishes, absent in the most primitive sharks, but common in more derived forms.
facts.quote: These fin spines are found only in primitive jawed fishes and are apparently absent from the most primitive sharks, but present in abundance in more derived forms.

facts.statement: Most Psarolepis fossils were discovered at the Yulongsi, Xishancun, and Xitun Formations, located about 10 km northwest of Qujing, Yunnan, China.
facts.quote: Most of the fossils of Psarolepis were discovered at the same locality of the Yulongsi, Xishancun and Xitun Formations, about 10 km northwest of the city of Qujing, Yunnan, China.

facts.statement: Remains of Psarolepis were collected in 1981 and 1984 by paleontologist Min Zhu and colleagues and dated to the Early Devonian and Late Silurian periods.
facts.quote: The remains of Psarolepis were collected in 1981 and 1984 by paleontologist Min Zhu and colleagues and dated from Early Devonian and Late Silurian periods.

facts.statement: When first described in 1998, Psarolepis was classified as a sarcopterygian (lobe-finned fish) due to skull and jaw similarities to primitive lungfishes.
facts.quote: When Psarolepis was described for the first time in 1998, it was placed in the group of sarcopterygians (lobe-finned fishes) because the skull and jaws resemble those of primitive lungfishes.

facts.statement: In 2001, researchers Zhu and Schultze provided evidence suggesting Psarolepis was likely a basal bony fish.
facts.quote: Later, in 2001, Zhu and Schultze gave more basis to the theory that Psarolepis was probably a basal bony fish.

facts.statement: The Paleobiology Database lists the parent group of Psarolepis as Sarcopterygii.
Psarolepis is classified within the class Osteichthyes.
The time range for Psarolepis is recorded as 422.7 to 413.02 million years ago, spanning the Pridoli to Lochkovian periods.
facts.quote: Time range: Pridoli to Lochkovian (422.7 to 413.02 million years ago)
